prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The intended answer is **Timsort**: it is stable, comparison-based, has **O(n)** best-case time and **O(n log n)** worst-case time.

Strictly speaking, standard Timsort is **not in-place** in the usual O(1)-auxiliary-space sense; it uses additional memory. If “in-place” is meant strictly, no standard textbook algorithm commonly matches all of those properties.
